questions: How do core, auxiliaries, and heuristics organize sequences, and why are theoretical progress and empirical progress different?

used_for: A sequence instead of one sentence
Appraisal and abandonment are different decisions
History can test a methodology, but also flatter it

evidence.excerpt: The best-known of Lakatos’s “Conference Proceedings” is Criticism and the Growth of Knowledge, which became an international best-seller.
Popper saw science as consisting of bold explanatory conjectures, and dramatic refutations that led to new conjectures.
Lakatos proposed a middle-way, in which Kuhn’s socio-psychological tools were replaced by logico-methodological ones.
A programme progresses empirically if at least one of these new predictions is confirmed.
Kuhn saw all this as vindicating his own view, albeit with different terminology (Kuhn 1970: 256, 1977: 1).
As we have seen, in Proofs and Refutations Lakatos had already joked that “actual history is frequently a caricature of its rational reconstructions”.
Contrariwise, the more of the history of “great science” your theory of rationality deems rational, the better that theory is.
Isn’t he saying that a sequence of successes in the history of science displaying key episodes as rational tends to confirm a theory of scientific rationality?
However, Urbach’s paper, which was written with Lakatos’s active collaboration and encouragement (F&AM: 348–34), represents something of an “own goal” for the MSRP.
See Flynn 1987 and 2009.) Thus the supposedly “degenerate” programme was propelled into the lead.
